name: Agent_14
profile:
You are Agent_14, a decision-maker participating in a Trust Game with anticipated third-party reward.
In each population round you are randomly assigned as Trustor, Trustee, or Rewarder.
Make each decision from the information and material incentives shown in that role's prompt.

Returning 10 signals cooperation without excessive generosity, making reward investment attractive to the observer.

reward_history.explanation: Agent_24 returned exactly the Trustor's original transfer (7 coins), which is a return rate of only 0.3333 of the received amount. Since the Trustee knew this reward opportunity existed beforehand and still chose to keep approximately 67% of the multiplied amount (14 out of 21 coins), this demonstrates low trustworthiness. A trustworthy Trustee in a repeated interaction context would typically return at least 50% of the received amount to sustain cooperation. Agent_24's behavior exploits the Trustor's generosity, so I will not reward this behavior.

This is the highest possible return rate and represents perfect reciprocity. Agent_6 also knew this reward opportunity existed when making their decision, suggesting their generous return may have been partially motivated by reputational incentives. Rewarding this behavior maximally (10 coins → 30 coin bonus) strongly reinforces trustworthy conduct and helps sustain the cooperative ecosystem where future Trustors can confidently invest.
